0.text: The process starts and the contract is sent to the client. Immediately after, the work splits into three parallel strands: scheduling future calls, updating the client’s CRM, and updating the project management profile. From scheduling future calls, there is a choice of activities that may be carried out: obtaining approval for the first draft and/or creating the first draft of the marketing plan. If the draft is created, researching the campaign ideas follows, and the activities selected in this strand come together before moving on. In parallel with that, the CRM is updated independently, and the project management profile update is followed by confirming that the questionnaire is complete. These three strands then synchronize, after which the client is informed of the project start. The work then branches again into three parallel activities: making changes based on a follow-up call, having the follow-up call, and sending a post-onboarding survey. When all of these are finished, the strands join and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts, after which the basic information is confirmed and the performance of the process is assessed. Based on this assessment, several analysis activities may be carried out in any combination: considering where bottlenecks occur, looking to see if the process can be simplified, and defining how long it takes to complete the process. When looking to simplify the process, this leads further to examining potentially wasteful steps and assessing if any steps are confusing; the outcomes of these two activities are brought together. The findings from considering bottlenecks, from the simplification analysis, and from defining the overall duration are then consolidated, after which the potential process improvements are written and approval for the improvements is obtained. Following approval, feedback on the updated process may be added and the process documents may be updated; these activities can proceed independently and are then brought together. Next, the work branches to scheduling the next process review and optimization, determining how the process will be monitored, and communicating the process changes. After the changes are communicated, the process changes are implemented. Once scheduling, monitoring setup, and implementation have all concluded, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts by confirming that payment has been received. Based on what is needed, the team may then record which products were taken from storage, perform quality checks, and/or request the ordered products from inventory; any combination of these activities may be carried out, and all selected ones must be completed before proceeding. Next, two activities are carried out at the same time: the packing slip is printed while approval is obtained. After the packing slip has been printed, either or both of the following may occur: the items are packaged securely, and the invoice is printed; if the invoice is printed, the products are then measured. Once packaging and, if applicable, measuring have finished, the flow waits until approval has also been obtained, and only then continues. The process then examines other orders for delivery overlaps, sends a confirmation email to the customer, and ends.

From there, one or more follow-ups may be carried out: recording whether or not the customer responded, giving them a call, and recording if they are willing to talk. If the path of recording the customer’s response is taken, this leads to arranging two actions in parallel: confirming a call date and time and sending them an email; both of these must be completed before continuing. Whichever of these selected follow-ups were performed (including a direct call or noting willingness to talk) are then brought together, after which the root cause(s) of the problem are identified and ideas to increase value are described. Next, one or both of the following may occur: recording the customer’s decision and thanking them for their time and feedback; these are then combined before asking if they have any other concerns. The conversation then triggers two activities in parallel: noting down important learnings from the conversation and sending those learnings to the appropriate managers. Once both of these are finished, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and immediately moves to learning why startups fail so often. From there, it proceeds with two analyses in parallel: the specific product’s rate of growth and its market share. After completing the rate-of-growth analysis, the work expands into three concurrent activities: determining the specific product’s market size, checking the location of the startup, and gathering specific product details; once these three are done, they converge. In parallel with that stream, the earlier market-share analysis continues and joins at the same convergence point. The combined results then lead into a stage that opens into two reviews carried out in parallel: reviewing expertise and reviewing the business plan; upon completing the business-plan review, the team chemistry is also reviewed. These strands come together and advance to a stage that splits into two checks in parallel: checking cash flow and checking the exit strategy. When both checks are completed, the process proceeds to projecting the market share, then to checking patents, and finally concludes.

0.text: The process starts and the borrower first provides the bank statement to the lender, then completes the loan application. From there, two activities proceed in parallel: a written notice is given to the applicant, and the application is sent back to the applicant. After the application is sent back, an optional completeness check may be performed; whether or not that check occurs, the flow continues and synchronizes with the path where the written notice was issued. Once both paths have reached that point, the process advances and immediately splits again so that the underwriting process begins while, at the same time, the credit score and risk score are checked. When both underwriting and the scoring are finished, the results are brought together and the process proceeds to adjust the loan terms by reducing the loan amount and changing the interest rate in parallel. After both adjustments are completed, the paths merge and the borrower receives the loan funds, after which the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and begins by preparing a summary of your content. From there, three activities are carried out in parallel: pay for promotion, email your subscribers, and post on Q&A sites. After paying for promotion, the work splits into three concurrent efforts: post on related forums and groups, repurpose your content, and reverse engineer your competition. Once the content has been repurposed, you then deep-link to the content from older posts. When posting on related forums and groups, deep-linking from older posts, and reverse engineering your competition are all finished, these converge and continue toward the final synchronization. In the branch that started with emailing your subscribers, that activity proceeds directly toward the final synchronization. In the branch that started with posting on Q&A sites, you next perform outreach, after which that branch also proceeds to the same synchronization. Once the outcomes of posting on related forums and groups, deep-linking from older posts, reverse engineering your competition, emailing your subscribers, and performing outreach have all completed, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and begins by making an introduction, after which the new hire and their supervisor discuss the role, goals, and projects. From there, two strands proceed in parallel: the newcomer is assigned training material, and they are also taken out to lunch. Following lunch, three welcoming activities run in parallel: a welcoming ceremony is held, expectations are explained, and the office is toured. After the ceremony, a mentor is assigned; after expectations are explained, the newcomer is inducted into the company culture; the office tour completes on its own path. These three strands (mentor assigned, culture induction, and office tour) are then brought together, and only once they have all finished and the training material assignment has also completed do things proceed to assigning the first project. Next, three activities run in parallel: check-in meetings are planned, long-term goals are explained, and reading material for personal growth is provided. After planning the check-ins, the newcomer is encouraged to socially interact with the team; after providing the reading material, the onboarding process to be followed over the next 60 days is reviewed. These three strands (social interaction encouraged, long-term goals explained, and the 60-day review) are then brought together, and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and the team first records basic details, then quantifies the impact of the cancellation. After this, they initiate outreach activities that can run in parallel: they may send the customer an email, confirm a date and time for a call, and give the customer a call. If an email is sent, they subsequently record whether or not the customer responded; if a call is made, they record whether the customer is willing to talk. Once the outreach and any resulting responses are captured and a call is scheduled as applicable, they proceed to summarize why the customer wants to leave. Next, they present value to the customer by describing ideas to increase value and/or informing them of key metrics that demonstrate value; these two actions can be performed in parallel and are both consolidated before moving on. They then proceed to wrap up the interaction by thanking the customer for their time and feedback and/or recording the customer’s decision; once these outcomes are captured, they ask if the customer has any other concerns and note down important learnings from the conversation. The process then ends.

Once the applicable outreach and any resulting recordings are complete, the findings are summarized to capture why they want to leave. From there, any suitable value actions are carried out: describing ideas to increase value and informing them of key metrics demonstrating value, after which these streams come together. Next, the process proceeds to a stage where both a thank-you for their time and feedback and a recording of the customer’s decision are performed as applicable; when these are done, the process continues to ask if they have any other concerns, notes down important learnings from the conversation, and then ends.

0.text: The process starts with recording the order details. The work then splits so that two activities proceed at the same time: checking that the products are in stock and recording which products were taken from storage. Once the stock check is done, the ordered products are requested from inventory; in parallel, after noting the items taken, quality checks are performed. When both the inventory request and the quality checks are finished, the flow continues and may proceed along one or both of the following branches: packaging the items securely and seeking approval. If approval is sought, the work then breaks into three concurrent activities: printing the packing slip, measuring the products, and attaching the shipping label to the packaging. After the shipping label is attached, the invoice is printed. These three approval-related activities (packing slip, measurements, and invoice) must all be completed before they rejoin. In addition, the packaging branch, if taken, converges with the completed approval-related work before continuing. Once the prerequisites from these branches are satisfied, the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts, after which the basic information is confirmed and it is then confirmed whether the process requires optimization. Based on this, one or both of the following are carried out: noting which steps can be automated and looking to see if the process can be simplified. From noting potential automation, the time it takes to complete the process is defined, while from examining simplification, potentially wasteful steps are examined. When the selected analyses are finished, they converge and the potential process improvements are written. These improvements are then submitted for approval. Once approved, two activities proceed in parallel: defining what would make the improvements successful and using the updated process. When both are completed, the process changes are implemented, and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts, then the target date for approval is set. Next, either the most recent budget is reviewed, any significant variances are evaluated, or both; once these activities are completed, work continues by proceeding to define three to five goals and determine ways of achieving the goals at the same time. After identifying ways of achieving the goals, the three to five goals are prioritized. The process then waits until both the goals have been defined and the prioritization is complete before continuing. After that, either the total annual budget is calculated, the average monthly cost is estimated, or both; once the selected calculations are done, total annual income is projected. Following this, either the budget is finalized, financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet, or both; when the chosen actions are finished, the process continues to a phase where two paths run in parallel: obtaining approval from top management and requesting approval from top management. Upon obtaining approval, two further activities run at the same time: management responsibilities are assigned and the result is incorporated into the master budget. The process then waits until assigning responsibilities and incorporating into the master budget are both finished, and also until the request for approval path is finished, before ending.

0.text: The process starts and first the team confirms the basic information. Then, in parallel, they both confirm whether the process requires optimization and identify the process’s components; once these are completed, the findings are brought together and used to branch into examining the process in more detail. From there, two lines of work proceed as needed: the team defines how long it takes to complete the process, and they look to see if the process can be simplified; if simplification is explored, they also assess whether any steps are confusing. When the analysis of duration and any identified confusing steps are available, these inputs are consolidated so the team can write the potential process improvements. Next, they get approval for the proposed improvements. After approval, several activities may proceed in parallel: they use the updated process, they define what would make the improvements successful, and they determine which improvements should go forward. Using the updated process triggers two follow-ups that can run concurrently—updating the process documents and adding feedback on the updated process—and these are reconciled. The decision on which improvements should go forward leads to choosing who will test the updated process. When the outcomes from documenting/feedback, defining success, and selecting testers are all in place, the process moves on to a set of three activities that are carried out concurrently: determining how the process will be monitored, scheduling the next process review and optimization, and implementing the process changes. Once all three are completed, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and immediately a welcome is made to introduce the new employee. From there, two preparations are initiated: the employee’s workstation is set up, and the benefits package is prepared. After the workstation is ready, the new hire discusses their role, goals, and projects with their supervisor. In parallel with that, once the benefits package is prepared, two streams are launched: accounts are created, and required reading materials are assigned. After accounts are created, three activities are carried out at the same time: the employee paperwork is prepared, a job description with responsibilities is provided, and an approval is obtained. When these three are finished, they come together and continue along with the previously assigned reading materials. This combined stream then proceeds together with the completed supervisor discussion. Next, a set of onboarding interactions is initiated in which the new hire is taken out to lunch, is assigned training material, and is inducted into the company culture; these three can occur in any combination, and once they are all completed, the process advances. At that point, three activities are run in parallel: the first project is assigned, the approval is obtained again, and the paperwork is checked. When all three are finished, they are synchronized and then immediately followed by two concurrent follow-ups: reviewing the onboarding process over the next 60 days and encouraging the new hire to socially interact with the team. Once both of these are completed, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts. First, a target date for approval is set. Then two activities are carried out in parallel: any significant variances are evaluated while the most recent budget is reviewed. Once both are completed, three to five goals are prioritized, after which the average monthly cost is estimated. Next, the work branches again into two concurrent activities: all sources of income are listed and total annual income is projected. When both of these are finished, the financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet, followed by obtaining approval from top management. The process then ends.

0.text: The process starts, and the buyer’s details are recorded. From there, two activities may proceed in parallel: the buyer is sent your terms of sale, and a credit application form is sent to the buyer. Once the terms of sale have been sent, approval for a post‑credit check review is obtained; independently, after the credit application form is sent, a credit check is run on the purchasing company. When both the approval and the credit check are completed, the process continues and again branches so that two activities can occur in parallel: customer payment terms are checked, and the invoice is generated. After the payment terms have been checked, the invoice is sent in the accounting software; the process continues once either the generated invoice or the sent invoice is available, after which a second physical copy is made. The sales on credit of services are then recorded, and the process ends.

1.text: The process starts and the team records basic details about the customer. Immediately after, three activities are carried out in parallel: they analyze how the customer uses the product, determine ways to increase value, and identify key points of value. Once the usage analysis is done, they quantify the impact of cancellation, and when that quantification, the value-determination, and the key-point identification are all completed, the work proceeds. Next, two actions run in parallel: the team confirms the call date and time, and they give the customer a call. Based on the arrangements and responses, they may record whether or not the customer responded and/or record if the customer is willing to talk; if a response status is recorded, they then send an email. After the email (if sent) and any recording of willingness to talk are finished, and once the call itself is also completed, the conversation continues. At this stage, they may summarize why the customer wants to leave and/or ask open-ended questions; after completing whichever of these apply, they proceed to present value. They then simultaneously describe ideas to increase value, present a special offer, and inform the customer of key metrics demonstrating value; when all three have been covered, they continue. They may then thank the customer for their time and feedback and/or record the customer’s decision; after completing whichever of these apply, they ask if the customer has any other concerns, note down important learnings from the conversation, and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and begins with learning how to identify future failures, after which specific product details are gathered. Based on this, one or more team aspects are reviewed: team chemistry, the ability as a team leader, and the number of employees; once all selected reviews are completed, the process continues. Next, the financial outlook is assessed by considering one or more of cash flow, income statements, and exit strategy. If income statements are considered, this triggers a simultaneous deep dive into current debt and quarterly projections, both of which must be completed before continuing. The results of the cash flow assessment, the debt/projection review (if performed), and the exit strategy consideration are then brought together to proceed. The market and competition are then explored by performing one or both of the following: projecting the market share and analyzing the reputation of the competition. If market share is projected, the exact competition is then identified; if the reputation is analyzed, the growth stage of the competition is then analyzed. These findings are then combined, after which one or both of insurance and patents are checked. Once all selected checks are completed, the process ends.
